facts.fact: Voice of Nigeria reports that in Gombe State births are to be registered on tablets, every birth at a primary health centre captured 'immediately and electronically' and ward focal persons with devices recording births notified to them, per UNICEF and the National Population Commission; deaths are mentioned only as data the system would keep. No event date is given, so the published date is used.

Voice of Nigeria reports that Gombe State is positioned as a 'pilot hub' for digital birth registration, with representatives of 114 health facilities and 114 wards trained as trainers in a three-day workshop on using digital devices to register births, per UNICEF and the National Population Commission; no total of registration points is given and the published date is used.

Voice of Nigeria reports a National Population Commission technical expert describing the digital birth registration system as 'our Vital Reg', in a campaign UNICEF launched in collaboration with the Commission in Gombe State; the published date is used.

Voice of Nigeria reports that UNICEF and the National Population Commission launched a digital birth registration campaign in Gombe State after a three-day train-the-trainers workshop for 114 health facilities and 114 wards; the launch is undated in the text, so the published date is used.

systems.tiers: Gombe State: 114 health facilities (primary health centres) and 114 wards (ward focal persons with tablets)
